newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government clears new banking law draft.
newsitem.headline: Polish government clears new banking law draft.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a draft banking law which introduces European Union standards to the sector and allows banks to operate more safely, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.
"The government approved a draft banking law... which aims at improving the security of banks' operations and harmonising (banking) regulations with EU standards," Belka said.
"It is a new constitution for the banking system," he told a news conference.
Central Bank Deputy President Witold Kozinski said the bill, which the bank fully supported, would help in the fight against money laundering.
"We will be better equipped to combat what we call money laundering," Kozinski told the same conference.
The new bill, if passed by parliament and signed into law by the president, would replace current regulations from the early 1990s.
It would reduce to 15 percent from 25 percent of shareholder equity the top value of the equity investments that each bank can make.

The draft also introduces more stringent rules on the acquisition of shares in banks by introducing a requirement for the central bank to give permission for any purchase of stock giving more than five percent of votes.
The National Bank of Poland's (NBP) permission is now required to execute more than 10 percent of votes.
But the bill also gives banks more room to expand their core lending activities by increasing to 25 percent from 10 percent of shareholder equity the limit on credit exposure to a single borrower.

The bill paves the way for a reform in banking supervision, long a bone of contention between the government, which wanted it separated from the NBP, and the bank which had wanted to keep supervision within its structures.
The current proposal leaves banking supervision in the central bank but subordinates it to a future Banking Supervision Committee, which has yet to be created.

The committee would be chaired by the NBP's president and would include representatives of the NBP, the finance ministry, the presidential chancellery, the securities commission and the banking guarantee fund.
"Under the new plan, banking supervision is situated within NBP structures and is controlled by the Banking Supervision Commission," Belka said.
